newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Japan, U.S. still far apart on insurance - Barshefsky.
newsitem.headline: Japan, U.S. still far apart on insurance - Barshefsky.

text.p: Japan and the United States remain remain "very far apart" in negotiations to reach an agreement on liberalising Japan's insurance market, U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said on Monday.
"I believe we remain very far apart," Barshefsky told a news conference at the World Trade Organisation's (WTO) first ministerial conference in Singapore.
The United States and Japan have been intensely negotiating since last week to resolve their dispute over insurance liberalisation before a self-imposed December 15 deadline.

Barshefsky said U.S. Trade Representative negotiator Ira Shapiro would be coming to Singapore from Tokyo later on Monday, and she would decide sometime later whether to return to Tokyo herself after the WTO meeting this week for further insurance talks.
"I would say that going back to Tokyo does frankly not necessarily indicate either that we think there will be an agreement or that there won't."
Barshefsky's comments were in line with what a senior Japanese Finace Ministry official told reporters in Tokyo on Monday.
The disagreement between the two nations centres on U.S. charges that Japan is planning to renege on a 1994 trade agreement on the deregulation of its lucrative insurance market.

Washington has argued that the agreement calls for Tokyo to deregulate the huge primary life and casualty insurance sector, which is dominated by Japanese companies, before unleashing competition in the tiny specialty insurance market.
